tip: Put 'en' before an adjective for the most: 'en sıcak' means hottest. 'en sıcak günü', the hottest day.
Verb + -mişti marks an earlier past, had done: 'izlemiştim' means I had watched it before, prior to now.
'siz' is the polite or plural you and its verb ends in -sunuz: 'bekliyorsunuz' means you wait, matching 'siz'.
'ile' after a noun means by means of: 'feribot ile' means by ferry. It can also contract to 'feribotla'.
For we need to, use verb+me plus -miz plus 'gerekiyor': 'gitmemiz gerekiyor' means we need to go.
'lazım' means needed or necessary and follows the thing required: 'bilet lazım' means a ticket is needed.
Many verbs pair a noun with 'etmek' (to do): 'tercüme etmek' means to translate, so 'tercüme ediyor' is she is translating.
The bare verb stem is the command form for 'sen': 'al' means take. 'şemsiyeni al', take your umbrella.
Adding -t makes a verb mean to make someone do it: 'gülümsetiyor' means makes one smile, from 'gülümse' (smile).
Add -ca/-ce to an adjective to form an adverb: 'hızlı' (fast) becomes 'hızlıca', meaning quickly.
'sayende' is a set phrase meaning thanks to you, crediting someone for a good result: 'senin sayende', thanks to you.
Insert -ama before the ending for cannot: 'bırakamıyorum' means I can't put it down, from 'bırak' (leave, drop).
'daha' before an adjective means more, making the comparative: 'daha iyi' means better. The thing compared takes -den.
'hem ... hem' means both ... and, placed before each item: 'hem sağlıklı hem eğlenceli' means both healthy and fun.
Adding -ıl makes a verb passive: 'satmak' (to sell) becomes 'satılıyor', are being sold, with no named seller.
Verb + -dıkça means as or the more that happens: 'geçtikçe' means as it passes. 'yıllar geçtikçe', as the years go by.
'keşke' plus a -se verb voices a wish: 'dinse' = if only it would stop.
-le on a noun means by or with: 'otobüsle' ('otobüs' + le) = by bus, no separate word needed.
Insert -ebil for can or be able to: 'gidebilirim' = I can go, from 'git' (go), t softening to d before the vowel.
-ma plus a possessive makes a that-clause noun: 'varmamız' = our arriving, that we arrive.
Position words put the -nin ending on the noun: 'köprünün altından' ('köprü' + nün, 'alt' + ından) = from under the bridge.
-erek says by doing something: 'yürüyerek' ('yürü' + yerek) = by walking, describing how you go.
-malı means must or have to: 'hazırlamalıyız' ('hazırla' + malı + yız) = we must prepare.
After a number the noun stays singular: 'altı sandalye' = six chairs, 'sandalye' not 'sandalyeler'.
-dik plus a possessive makes a which-clause: 'gezdiğimiz yerler' ('gez' + diğimiz) = the places that we visited.
Add -ın for a polite or plural command: 'kapatın' = close (formal), versus plain 'kapat' to one friend.
-ince means when or as soon as: 'gelince' ('gel' + ince), so 'bahar gelince' = once spring comes.
'hem ... hem' frames both ... and: 'hem sağlıklı hem ekonomik' = both healthy and economical.
'meğer' plus a -miş verb marks a fact you just realized: 'gitmiş' = turns out he had gone, not eyewitnessed.
-erdi marks a past habit, used to: 'giderdik' = we used to go ('git' softens to gid before the vowel), 'yüzerdik' = we used to swim.
